articles.title: Import AI 469: Science AI; RSI simulator; and Zuck's technological pessimism
articles.titleZh: Import AI 469：科学 AI；RSI 模拟器；扎克伯格的技术悲观主义
articles.author: Jack Clark

zh.thesis: 当前 AI 在发现未知规则上仍远逊于人类，但接近的进展可能触发自我改进的临界点。
paragraphs: DiG-bench 用 70 个隐藏规则的游戏测试 AI 的探索发现能力。顶级模型如 Opus 5 只在最难的第 7 层达到 20% 成功率，而人类能全部通关。
这衡量的是模型能否通过试错推断环境规律，正是创造力的前提。作者预测 2027 年中达到人类水平，届时递归自我改进可能加速。
Inherent 公司的 Faraday 模型用 27B 参数监督大型模型，在复现论文实验中超过 Opus 4.8 和 GPT-5.5，显示了科学研究的品味。
扎克伯格在《未来属于每个人》中主张普及超级智能以平衡权力，但回避了关键问题：一个能超人发明的系统会甘于为个体赋能吗？
作者认为扎克伯格的技术乐观主义可能忽视发明能力的颠覆性。这期 Newsletter 本身是链接合集，但各条都指向值得深思的 AI 前沿。

en.thesis: AI is still far behind humans at discovering unknown rules, but approaching that level could trigger a self-improvement tipping point.
paragraphs: DiG-bench tests AI's ability to explore and discover using games with 70 hidden rules. Top models like Opus 5 only reach a 20% success rate on the hardest level 7, while humans can clear all of them.

This measures whether a model can infer environmental regularities through trial and error, which is the precondition for creativity. The authors predict human-level performance by mid-2027, at which point recursive self-improvement might accelerate.
Inherent's Faraday model uses 27B parameters to supervise larger models and surpasses Opus 4.8 and GPT-5.5 in reproducing paper experiments, showing taste in scientific research.

In 'The Future Belongs to Everyone,' Zuckerberg argues for democratizing superintelligence to balance power, but sidesteps the key question: would a system that can out-invent humans be content to empower individuals?

The author thinks Zuckerberg's technological optimism may overlook the disruptive nature of inventiveness. This newsletter is itself a collection of links, yet each points to an AI frontier worth pondering.

articles.title: Epictetus Ran a Better Productivity System Than Any App You’ve Bought
articles.titleZh: Epictetus 运营着比任何你买过的应用都更好的生产力系统
articles.author: JA Westenberg

zh.thesis: 生产力工具的问题不在工具，而在它们默认一切都该由你负责；Epictetus 的管辖范围法则是更好的过滤器。
paragraphs: 市面上的生产力系统都默认你是个失职的人：你的效率低下，因为你的问题。于是它们给你更好的收件箱、更聪明的数据库、更丰富的标签，但压力还是在你身上。
Epictetus 是斯多葛学派哲学家，曾是奴隶。他的系统不从「如何管理更多」出发，而从一个问题开始：什么是归你管的？
他只关注三样东西：你的判断、你的欲望、你的决定。别人的行动、意见、情绪，还有你无法改变的算法和市场，都不在管辖范围内。捕获意味着接受责任，把噪音变成任务。
现代工作模糊了这条界线：收件箱是别人的输出队列，任务列表里混着别人的请求。工具的理论是「看见就是掌控」，但 Epictetus 说：你只对同意和拒绝负责。
所以真正的问题不是「怎么管理更多」，而是「这是不是我的」。如果归你，就行动；如果不归，就不捕获、不追踪。系统再完美，也不能让你替别人做决定。

en.thesis: Productivity tools don't fail because of the tools; they assume everything is your responsibility. Epictetus's circle of control is a better filter.
paragraphs: Productivity systems out there all assume you're failing: your low efficiency is your fault. So they give you better inboxes, smarter databases, richer tags, but the pressure is still on you.
Epictetus was a Stoic philosopher and a former slave. His system doesn't start from 'how to manage more' but from one question: what is up to you?

He only pays attention to three things: your judgments, your desires, your decisions. Other people's actions, opinions, emotions, and algorithms and markets you can't change are not in your control. Capturing means accepting responsibility, turning noise into tasks.

Modern work blurs this line: the inbox is others' output queue, the to-do list mixes in others' requests. The tools' theory is 'seeing is controlling,' but Epictetus says: you are only responsible for agreeing and refusing.
So the real question is not 'how to manage more' but 'is this mine?' If it's yours, act; if it's not, don't capture, don't track. No matter how perfect the system, it can't make decisions for others.

articles.title: Am I better because of AI?
articles.author: dreamreal

zh.thesis: 把自我写进 prompt，能让 AI 更懂你，但变好与否取决于要不要把工具当作拐杖。
paragraphs: 作者反思 AI 是否让他变得更好。他承认自己写代码和文章更快了，因为 AI 像即时的对话伙伴，既没有偏见，也不嫌他问题蠢。
可这只是一时的印象——没有 AI，这些优势就消失。像工匠离开作坊，生产效率就掉回去，所以答案取决于工具的持续可用性。
他的方法是把人生观、价值观、性格缺陷全写进 prompt。AI 说这些细节不是用来查询的，而是决定回答空间的形状，让输出不再平庸。
但作者担心，这更像是在讨好自己——越了解你，就越容易迎合你。他必须明确要求反驳，否则 AI 只会做更好的镜子，而不是有用的镜子。
所以真正的问题不是「我是否更好了」，而是「有没有变得更清晰」，因为他发现写 prompt 让他更了解自己。这就是成长，哪怕 AI 只是催化剂。

en.thesis: Putting yourself into the prompt helps AI understand you, but whether you become better depends on whether you lean on the tool as a crutch.
paragraphs: The author reflects on whether AI has made him better. He admits he writes code and articles faster now, because AI is like an instant conversation partner — it has no biases and never thinks his questions are stupid.

But that is just a temporary impression: without AI, those advantages vanish. Like a craftsman leaving his workshop, productivity drops back down, so the answer depends on the tool's constant availability.

His method is to write his worldview, values, and character flaws all into the prompt. AI says these details are not for querying but for shaping the space of possible answers, so the output is no longer mediocre.

But he worries this is more like flattering himself — the more it knows you, the easier it is to pander. He has to explicitly ask for pushback, or else AI will only be a better mirror, not a useful one.
So the real question is not 'am I better?' but 'have I become clearer?', because he finds that writing prompts makes him understand himself more. That is growth, even if AI is just the catalyst.

articles.title: Pluralistic: Jennifer Jenkins' 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' (17 Aug 2026)
articles.titleZh: Pluralistic：珍妮弗·詹金斯的《音乐版权、创造力与文化》
articles.author: Cory Doctorow

zh.thesis: 音乐版权法是一堆临时拼凑的规则，远比人们想象的更随意，而詹金斯的教科书能把它讲清楚。
paragraphs: 詹金斯是美国杜克大学公共领域研究中心的主任，每年负责整理进入公共领域的作品清单。她最出名的是把复杂的版权法讲得既明白又有趣，关于米老鼠版权到期的解释是公认最好的。
她与丈夫博伊尔合著了《音乐版权、创造力与文化》第二版，现在开放获取。书里融合了学术和通俗写法，从古代讲到现在，说明今天关于谁该付费、何时要许可的规矩并非天经地义，一直在变。
书中穿插了她们自己的漫画《盗窃！一部音乐史》，还有大量链接到音乐片段，让阅读生动起来。特别值得看的是对艾德·希兰、凯蒂·佩里和法瑞尔·威廉姆斯诉讼的分析，这些案子都涉及类似的旋律感觉，暴露了音乐版权法内在的矛盾。
版权法是随着新技术一次次临时补丁堆起来的，几乎没人真懂，但詹金斯懂。作者说自己从 1990 年代末就研究这些，读这本书仍每页都有新收获。

en.thesis: Music copyright law is a pile of ad-hoc rules, far more arbitrary than people think, and Jenkins's textbook makes it clear.
paragraphs: Jenkins is the director of Duke University's Center for the Study of the Public Domain, and she compiles the annual list of works entering the public domain. She's best known for explaining complex copyright law in a way that's both clear and entertaining; her explanation of Mickey Mouse's copyright expiration is widely considered the best.

She co-authored the second edition of 'Music Copyright, Creativity, and Culture' with her husband Boyle, and it's now open access. The book blends academic and popular writing, covering from ancient times to the present, and shows that today's rules about who pays and when you need a license are not set in stone—they've always been changing.

The book includes their own comic 'Theft! A History of Music' and lots of links to music clips, which makes reading lively. Particularly worth a look is their analysis of the lawsuits against Ed Sheeran, Katy Perry, and Pharrell Williams—all cases involving similar melodic feels—which expose the inherent contradictions in music copyright law.

Copyright law has been patched together one emergency fix at a time with each new technology, and almost no one really understands it, but Jenkins does. The author says she's been researching these issues since the late 1990s, but still finds something new on every page of this book.

articles.title: How a solo founder used Codex and ChatGPT to launch a fashion brand without engineers | Yana Welinder
articles.titleZh: Codex 如何帮一个独立创始人推出时尚品牌
articles.author: Claire Vo

zh.thesis: AI 工具已经能让一个没有工程师的创始人，从草图到建站全流程独自完成。
paragraphs: Yana Welinder 是 Yana Bana 品牌的独立创始人，把 AI 当作技术合伙人。她不会写代码，却用 ChatGPT 和 Codex 做出了一个时尚品牌，包含 3D 服装设计、电商网站和支付系统。
她的秘诀是把设计需求写成一份详细的「时尚提示词」，涵盖轮廓、面料、垂坠感和声音。这份提示词就像技术规格书，让 AI 生成的设计始终一致、逼真。
她还用 Codex 的计算机操作能力，去操控她从未学过的 CLO 3D 服装设计软件。AI 代替她完成了 CAD 文件的制作，相当于把专业软件的门槛也拆掉了。
整个流程从她的手绘草图开始，到模特照片、跑秀照片、甚至网红照片，都在一次 AI 会话中完成。就连供应商联系，也是用深度研究和浏览器自动化搞定的。
所以这件事的意义在于：过去需要工程师、设计师和供应商的活，现在一个创始人加 AI 就能起头。她还在并行测试人类打版师和 Codex 的效果，但风向已经很明显了。

en.thesis: AI tools already let a founder with no engineers go from sketch to live site entirely on their own.
paragraphs: Yana Welinder is the solo founder of Yana Bana, and she treats AI as her technical co-founder. She doesn't know how to code, yet she used ChatGPT and Codex to build a fashion brand, including 3D clothing design, an e-commerce site, and a payment system.

Her trick is to write design requirements as a detailed 'fashion prompt' covering silhouette, fabric, drape, and even sound. That prompt acts like a spec sheet, so the AI's output stays consistent and realistic.

She also used Codex's computer-use ability to drive CLO 3D, a clothing design software she had never learned. AI made the CAD files for her, which means the barrier of professional software is gone too.

The whole process starts with her hand-drawn sketch and goes to model photos, runway shots, even influencer photos, all in one AI session. Even supplier outreach was handled with deep research and browser automation.

So the takeaway is this: what used to need engineers, designers, and suppliers can now be started by one founder plus AI. She is still running a side-by-side test of human pattern makers versus Codex, but the direction is clear.

articles.title: Ban on Chinese robots leaves U.S. startups stranded
articles.titleZh: 对中国机器人的禁令让美国初创公司陷入困境
articles.author: Viola Zhou

zh.thesis: 美国政府对进口机器人的禁令过于激进，因为国内供应链尚未建立，反而可能扼杀初创公司。
paragraphs: 美国 FCC 上个月将外国制造的机器人列入黑名单，新机型必须在美组装且 65% 的零件价值来自国内，2029 年这一比例将升至 75%。禁令剑指中国，但已在美国销售的旧机型不受影响。
初创公司一片叫苦。比如 CosmicBrain AI 的创始人说，连苹果都在中国生产，机器人更复杂，在美国造根本不可能。他的公司已在加拿大设厂，但零件仍来自中国，不合规。
做美妆机器人的 Gemma 创始人也说，在美国根本无法快速打样，如果中国这条路断了，政府得拿出激励措施来。
也有公司支持禁令，比如 Agility Robotics 和 Nori Robotics，认为这能保护他们免受中国低价竞争，还能把科研订单引向本土。但批评者指出，当前只给了大棒，没有胡萝卜。
所以问题在于，政府一心想切断依赖，却忽略了替代品还不存在。禁令可能让初创公司买不起零件，拖慢美国机器人创新。

en.thesis: The U.S. government's ban on imported robots is too aggressive because the domestic supply chain isn't ready, and it may end up stifling startups.
paragraphs: Last month, the U.S. FCC blacklisted foreign-made robots. New models must be assembled in the U.S. with 65% of their parts' value coming from domestic sources, and by 2029 that share rises to 75%. The ban targets China, but older models already sold in the U.S. are unaffected.

Startups are complaining loudly. For example, the founder of CosmicBrain AI says even Apple makes its products in China, and robots are more complex, so building in the U.S. is simply impossible. His company has already set up a factory in Canada, but the parts still come from China, so they don't comply.
The founder of Gemma, which makes beauty robots, also says you can't quickly prototype in the U.S. If the Chinese route is cut off, the government needs to offer incentives.

There are also companies that support the ban, like Agility Robotics and Nori Robotics, arguing it protects them from cheap Chinese competition and directs research orders to domestic firms. But critics point out that the policy currently offers only a stick, not a carrot.
So the problem is that the government is determined to cut dependence, but forgets that no substitute exists yet. The ban may make parts unaffordable for startups, slowing U.S. robot innovation.

articles.title: Woke 1 is dead. We’ve learned nothing.
articles.titleZh: 「觉醒 1.0」死了，我们什么也没学到
articles.author: Matthew Yglesias

zh.thesis: 即使「觉醒 1.0」已落幕，其背后的结构性诱因仍在，而右翼的反噬只是重蹈覆辙。
paragraphs: 关于「觉醒 1.0 疯了」的讨论很多，作者认为这道歉不够诚恳，但这不是重点。更关键的是，它产生的结构性条件依然存在。
没有强把关人的世界，荒谬观念照样可以像野火一样蔓延，瞬间变成「共识」。机构领导虽不再被舆论绑架，但根子没除。
作者最恨的是那些「见风使舵」的人：他们明知对方疯，却不吭声，只求自保。预算专家知道「警察比学校花钱多」是假，却不说。
结果就是，说疯话的人倒霉，说真话的人更倒霉，只有「装傻」的人名利双收。这种激励结构至今没变，任何话题都可能跑偏。
如今右翼反噬，但并未纠偏「左派」的坏认知习惯，反而抛弃了关怀弱者，重演同样的毒性。作者担心，下一场风暴已在酝酿。

en.thesis: Even though 'Woke 1.0' is over, the structural causes that produced it remain, and the right-wing backlash is just repeating the same mistakes.
paragraphs: There is a lot of talk about how 'Woke 1.0 went crazy.' The author thinks the apology is not sincere, but that is not the point. More important is that the structural conditions that produced it still exist.

In a world without strong gatekeepers, absurd ideas can still spread like wildfire and turn into 'consensus' in an instant. Institutional leaders are no longer held hostage by public opinion, but the root cause has not been removed.

What the author hates most are the people who 'trim their sails': they know the other side is crazy, but stay silent to protect themselves. Budget experts know that 'police cost more than schools' is false, yet they do not say so.

The result is that those who say crazy things get into trouble, those who tell the truth get into even more trouble, and only those who 'play dumb' reap the rewards. This incentive structure has not changed, and any topic can go off the rails.

Now the right-wing backlash is here, but it has not corrected the left's bad cognitive habits. Instead, it has abandoned caring for the weak and is replaying the same toxicity. The author worries that the next storm is already brewing.

articles.title: We Tracked a Shipment of Rare Books. It Ended at an Amazon AI Training Facility
articles.titleZh: 我们追踪了一箱稀有书籍，它最终进了亚马逊的 AI 训练设施
articles.author: Emanuel Maiberg

zh.thesis: 亚马逊在大规模购买图书，扫描它们作为 AI 训练数据，并在此过程中销毁书籍。
paragraphs: 404 Media 调查发现，亚马逊在大量购买图书，扫描后用于 AI 训练，书籍本身则被销毁。这一行为此前从未被报道。
记者在疑似会被 AI 公司收购的稀有书中放入追踪器，一路跟踪它到了内华达州拉斯维加斯的一个亚马逊仓库，编号 VGT3。
仓库员工说，这里的工作就是接收大批印刷书籍，割掉装订以便更快扫描，书在这个过程中被毁。
仓库团队的 Logo 是一只恐龙，龇着牙，手里拿着一本书。报道还呼吁知情者提供更多线索。
所以这不是一次简单的物流追踪，而是揭露了 AI 训练数据来源的一面：为了喂饱模型，实体书籍正在被成批销毁。

en.thesis: Amazon is buying books in bulk, scanning them for AI training data, and destroying the books in the process.
paragraphs: An investigation by 404 Media has found that Amazon is buying up large numbers of books, scanning them for AI training, and then destroying the physical copies. This practice has never been reported before.
Journalists placed tracking devices in rare books suspected of being bought up by AI companies, and followed one all the way to an Amazon warehouse in Las Vegas, Nevada, numbered VGT3.
Warehouse employees say the work there is to receive large shipments of printed books, cut off the bindings for faster scanning, and the books are destroyed in the process.
The warehouse team's logo is a dinosaur, baring its teeth, holding a book. The report also calls for anyone with more information to come forward.
So this is not a simple logistics tracking, but a revelation of one side of AI training data sourcing: to feed the models, physical books are being destroyed in batches.

articles.title: Trump’s Bumbling, Racist Anti-China Protectionism Extends To Data Centers
articles.titleZh: 特朗普笨拙且种族主义的反华保护主义延伸到数据中心
articles.author: Karl Bode

zh.thesis: 特朗普政府的反华保护主义既腐败又无能，只会扰乱市场、抬高价格，而非保护安全。
paragraphs: 特朗普政府的反华政策一贯混乱，以国家安全为名，实际只是给科技市场带来混乱和涨价。从 TikTok 到华为，再到无人机，每次都以恐慌收场。
如今又要禁止数据中心使用中国硬件，包括光模块。报道提到这可能迫使 AWS 改用 Coherent 等美国厂商，推高云服务成本。
但政府一边说要强化网络安全，一边又在拆解监管机构，削减人员。这种自相矛盾让政策难以执行，更像是在向企业收「保护费」。
民主党也常帮倒忙，比如密歇根州欲禁中国电动车入境。作者认为正确的做法是让中国产品竞争，同时加强本国监管，但美国企业不愿面对竞争。
作者最终的观点是：即便保护主义是合理的（事实并非如此），这届政府也太腐败无能，无法成事。媒体却总忽略这一点。

en.thesis: Trump's anti-China protectionism is both corrupt and incompetent, and it only disrupts markets and raises prices, not protect security.
paragraphs: Trump's anti-China policies have always been chaotic. They invoke national security, but in practice they just bring chaos and price hikes to the tech market. From TikTok to Huawei, and then to drones, every time it ends in panic.
Now they want to ban Chinese hardware, including optical modules, from data centers. The report notes this could force AWS to switch to American vendors like Coherent, driving up cloud service costs.

But the administration talks about strengthening cybersecurity while dismantling regulatory agencies and cutting staff. This contradiction makes the policy hard to enforce, and it looks more like charging companies 'protection money'.

Democrats often make things worse, like Michigan wanting to ban Chinese electric vehicles. The author thinks the right approach is to let Chinese products compete while strengthening domestic regulation, but American companies don't want to face competition.
The author's final point is: even if protectionism were justified (which it isn't), this administration is too corrupt and incompetent to pull it off. Yet the media keeps ignoring this.

articles.title: Things you cannot buy in America?
articles.author: Tyler Cowen

zh.thesis: 美国买不到外置卷帘，因为它的房屋结构和供应链从根本上不兼容。
paragraphs: 欧洲很多住宅在窗户外面装一体式卷帘，能完全遮光，还能隔热。睡在真正的全黑房间里，是多数美国人从没体验过的事。
美国不是没人想要，而是这种卷帘得在建房子时就装进去。美国的木框架、护墙板、石膏板结构装不了，也就没有配套的供应链。
作者还列了其他美国难买的东西，比如草屋顶，但他自己对这类说法也持保留态度。这篇更像一个「潜在受阻市场」的有趣清单。
所以它给不出实质结论：每条都是点到为止的观察，真正的价值在于引发思考——为什么有些日常用品在一个国家就是买不到。

en.thesis: America lacks external roller shutters because its housing structure and supply chain are fundamentally incompatible.
paragraphs: Many European homes have integrated roller shutters on the outside of windows, which block out light completely and provide insulation. Sleeping in a truly pitch-black room is something most Americans have never experienced.

It's not that Americans don't want them, but these shutters have to be built into the house during construction. America's wood-frame, siding, and drywall structures can't accommodate them, so there's no supporting supply chain.

The author also lists other things that are hard to buy in America, like thatched roofs, but he's skeptical of such claims himself. This piece reads more like an interesting list of 'potentially blocked markets'.
So it doesn't offer any solid conclusions: each item is just a passing observation, and the real value is in sparking thought — why some everyday items simply can't be bought in one country.

zh.thesis: 这些书各有亮点，但其中几本令人失望。
paragraphs: 第一本写略萨的传记，讲他的私生活很带劲，如果想了解思想史或拉美文学就别看了，作者自己也觉得失望。
第二本写希腊和近东历史，作者试图讲清现实，这在同类书里难得。第三本写普罗科菲耶夫妻子的故事，比写音乐家本人的传记更有悬念。
第四本是古典文学评论集，作者虽受争议，但文笔和思想都属上乘，尤其论《奥德赛》译本的篇目值得一读。
第五本是科幻小说，风格有点怪但有趣，作者还没决定要不要继续读。
这份书单的意义在于参考，每本书具体如何还得自己判断。

en.thesis: These books each have their strengths, but a few of them disappoint.
paragraphs: The first is a biography of Vargas Llosa. It tells the story of his private life vividly, but if you want intellectual history or Latin American literature, skip it. The author himself found it disappointing.

The second is about Greek and Near Eastern history. The author tries to explain the reality, which is rare in books of this kind. The third tells the story of Prokofiev's wife, and it has more suspense than a biography of the composer himself.

The fourth is a collection of essays on classical literature. The author is controversial, but the prose and thinking are top-notch, especially the piece on translations of the Odyssey, which is worth reading.
The fifth is a science fiction novel. The style is a bit odd but interesting, and the author hasn't decided whether to keep reading.
The point of this list is as a reference. How each book is, you have to judge for yourself.

zh.thesis: 索马里安全形势改善带来经济繁荣，但反叛活动减少的原因尚不明确。
paragraphs: 索马里现在安全多了，经济也热起来了。商务部长说生意红火，新楼不停盖，机场附近尤其密集。
达哈卜大厦今年要开张，26 层，有豪华公寓、商场、健身房和清真寺。它是建在 1993 年黑鹰坠落的地点边上，当年美军士兵的尸体被拖过街道。
附近还有家贝丹咖啡，是位从瑞典回来的索马里人开的，已经成了兴旺的泛非连锁。
但为什么袭击减少了，说法不一。政府说彻底关上了青年党的大门，智库研究者却归功于 CCTV 普及、警察用 iPad 查车牌、便衣大量上街这些琐碎措施。
所以这篇只是转述一条背景信息：更安全的地方会变得更繁荣。想了解详细分析，得去读《经济学人》原文。

en.thesis: Somalia is safer and more prosperous now, but why the attacks have dropped is not clear.
paragraphs: Somalia is much safer now, and the economy is heating up. The commerce minister says business is booming, new buildings are going up steadily, and the area around the airport is especially dense.

Dahabshiil Tower is opening this year. It has 26 floors, luxury apartments, a mall, a gym, and a mosque. It is built next to the site of the 1993 Black Hawk Down incident, where the bodies of US soldiers were dragged through the streets.
Nearby there is also a Beidan Coffee, opened by a Somali who came back from Sweden, and it has already become a thriving pan-African chain.

But why the attacks have decreased, opinions differ. The government says it has completely shut the door on Al-Shabaab, but think tank researchers credit trivial measures like the spread of CCTV, police using iPads to check license plates, and many plainclothes officers on the streets.
So this piece just relays a background fact: safer places become more prosperous. For detailed analysis, you need to read the Economist article.
